topics.title: Persian, Phoenician, Inca, Maya, and Aksum

facts.title: Ancient Greek city-states
facts.text: Communities across the ancient Greek world developed into city-states, including Athens and Sparta.

facts.title: Athenian democracy — historic scope
facts.text: Athens introduced democratic institutions around 510–507 BCE; this is a historic development, not a claim that ancient Athens met modern democratic standards.

facts.title: Hellenistic period
facts.text: The Hellenistic period is conventionally dated from about 323 to 31 BCE.

facts.title: Iliad and Odyssey — traditional attribution
facts.text: According to tradition, Homer composed the Iliad and the Odyssey around 750 BCE.

facts.title: Indus civilization — regional scope
facts.text: The Indus civilization flourished around five thousand years ago in parts of modern Afghanistan, Pakistan, and India.

facts.title: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro
facts.text: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are key archaeological sites associated with the Indus civilization.

facts.title: Indus material evidence
facts.text: Archaeological evidence for the Indus civilization includes seals, jewellery, weights and measures, and evidence related to drainage and water management.

facts.title: Roman civilization — Tiber context
facts.text: Ancient Rome developed on the Tiber River in the Italian peninsula.

facts.title: Roman Twelve Tables — historic legal record
facts.text: The Twelve Tables are an early Roman legal text traditionally dated to the mid-fifth century BCE.

facts.title: Ancient Chinese river context
facts.text: Early Chinese civilizations developed in river valleys including the Yellow River and Yangtze River regions.

facts.title: Inca civilization — Andean context
facts.text: The Inca civilization developed in the Andes of South America; Machu Picchu is an important Inca archaeological site in Peru.

facts.title: Maya civilization — Mesoamerican context
facts.text: The Maya civilization developed in Mesoamerica; Chichén Itzá is a major Maya archaeological site in present-day Mexico.

facts.title: Phoenician writing — historic scope
facts.text: Phoenician writing was an influential consonantal alphabetic script in the ancient Mediterranean; ‘first alphabet’ claims require more precise historical scope.

facts.title: Achaemenid Persia — historic scope
facts.text: The Achaemenid Empire was an ancient Persian empire; its history includes rulers such as Cyrus II and Darius I.

facts.title: Aksum — regional historic context
facts.text: The Kingdom of Aksum was an ancient polity in the Horn of Africa and the southern Arabian region, with a history of urban and commercial activity.

notes.title: Greek source-superlative boundary
notes.text: The scan’s claims about first maps, the greatest playwright, a cultural golden age, deities, and the Trojan War are not imported as unqualified historical facts.

notes.title: Indus attribution boundary
notes.text: Claims assigning the Indus civilization to one ethnicity, calling it first urbanization, or attributing an invention/discovery to one figure are withheld. Archaeological interpretation remains evidence-led and incomplete.

notes.title: Religious and ethnicity boundary
notes.text: Theological claims, ethnic naming, contemporary-population statements, and oldest/first language claims in the scan are withheld from unqualified learning records.

notes.title: Ancient-world source boundary
notes.text: Simplified religious doctrine, founder claims, first alphabet claims, and OCR-uncertain country/civilization claims are withheld unless precisely corroborated.

notes.title: Question-bank exclusion boundary
notes.text: All 13 printed MCQs are withheld in this pass: superlatives and legendary premises are excluded, while otherwise safe questions await individual authority-by-authority corroboration beyond the shared historical-source ledger.
